title: Pin resolver consolidation: define precedence and compatibility for tag/semver/hash pins
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Customers can pin models in three different ways today: immutable commit hashes, semver strings (exact or ranges), and mutable tags (eg. 'stable', 'latest', 'redwood/experimental'). Our current runtime SDK and API accept all three formats but the resolver behavior is underspecified, creating subtle surprises during rollouts and when clients mix pin formats. Goal: produce an unambiguous, implementable spec for the pin resolver used by the API and client SDKs, plus guidance for publishing performance profiles against pinned artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: A single resolver spec document that defines precedence when multiple pin forms are present
SDK helpers (JS/Python) that implement spec with identical behavior to server resolver
Integration tests covering common and edge cases (semver ranges, prerelease, tag drift, hash collisions)
Migration guidance for existing customers and compatibility mode toggles for backcompat
Perf profile publish API contract that ties profiles to immutable artifacts and exposes a lightweight tag->artifact registration flow
spec_summary: Recommended resolver precedence: 1) exact commit hash (40-char SHA or commit ref) — treated as canonical immutable identifier; 2) exact semver (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, optional build metadata) — resolves to the latest artifact that matches that exact version; 3) semver range (~, ^, >=, <=) — resolves to the highest satisfying released semver within the model's release set; 4) mutable tag (string without semver syntax) — resolves to the tag's current bound artifact and is explicitly documented as mutable. When multiple pin fields are supplied in the same request, the server fails fast unless an explicit precedence override header is provided; SDKs should surface a deterministic merge that mirrors server precedence and warn when mutability/range is used in high-SLO routes.
edge_cases_and_decisions: Pre-release versions (1.2.0-beta) are excluded from semver range resolution by default unless the requester opts-in via an 'include_prerelease' flag.

Tag drift: tags that move are allowed but publishing a performance profile requires binding the profile to an immutable artifact (commit or exact semver). The server stores both the profile->artifact link and a tag->artifact snapshot for history queries.
Range semantics: we use npm-style semver precedence for range parsing. If multiple artifacts satisfy a range, choose the highest semver by build metadata-agnostic comparison.
Fallbacks: if a semver range has no match and a 'fallback_tag' is provided, attempt that tag; otherwise return 404 with a clear resolution error code.
Hash validation: commit-hash pins must match a canonical 40-hex SHA; short hashes are allowed in SDKs but expanded via the service. Ambiguous short-hash resolution returns a multi-match error.
Signed manifests: in environments requiring tamper-evidence, the resolver verifies signed manifest fingerprints before resolving tag->artifact mappings.
Caching: resolved artifact IDs are cached per pin expression and namespace for 5 minutes by default; SDKs expose cache TTL and allow opt-out for debug paths.
Telemetry: every resolution emits a telemetry event with pin_type, resolved_artifact, resolution_latency, and whether fallback occurred. Telemetry must not contain model weights or other PII.

Performance profile publishing: publishing requires immutable-artifact binding. When a user publishes a profile with a tag, the service resolves the tag to the current artifact and records both the artifact id and the tag at publish time. Profile reads can query by artifact, tag, or semver range; tag queries are translated to the artifact snapshot at publish time for historical accuracy.
implementation_notes: API: extend the model resolution endpoint to return both 'resolved_artifact_id' and 'resolution_trace' (string) documenting which rule applied. Keep response stable and minimal; large traces should be stored in logs rather than responses.
SDKs: add ModelPin.resolve(pinExpression, options) that mirrors server precedence and returns resolution metadata; deprecate existing ad-hoc helpers in favor of a single entrypoint.
Runtime: resolver must be idempotent and safe under concurrent tag updates; implement CAS or revisioned tag records in the DB.
Perf profiles: add artifact_id as required field when creating a profile; server-side convenience: if a tag is supplied, resolve and return artifact_id in create response.

Backward compatibility: default to 'compatibility' mode for 3 releases with a log-only rollout of strict failure behavior. Expose an account-level flag for strict_mode to fail-fast on mixed-pin requests.
Docs: publish a migration guide and an SDK changelog calling out the new warnings and the opt-in strict_mode toggle.
comments: 2025-01-16: Initial discovery notes — customers reported two incidents where 'stable' moved during a canary, causing unseen perf regressions. Letting tags be mutable is necessary for fast iteration, but we need stronger tooling to make that explicit.
2025-01-20: Design sync — agreed on precedence ordering and that commit-hash should be treated as authoritative. PM asked for a user-friendly error code when a range resolves to nothing.

2025-01-24: Engineering review — Tomas prototyped SDK resolve helper. Found ambiguity in current API response shape; we will add 'resolution_trace' (short string) and keep large traces in internal logs.
2025-01-28: Security review request submitted — mocked up signed manifest verification flow. Security asked for threat model doc before sign-off (link in artifacts).
2025-02-01: PR opened for server resolver changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/834. Includes unit tests for semver range and prerelease opt-in.
2025-02-02: PM feedback — add explicit migration paragraph and a 3-release grace period for strict-mode. Also request a small dashboard tile to surface 'tag drift' events for customer teams.

publish SDK helpers in JS and Python, include opt-in include_prerelease flag
add integration tests and a small e2e where a tag moves mid-rollout to verify telemetry and rollback paths
create migration docs and customer-facing FAQ
instrument dashboard tile for tag-drift alerts and a policy to notify affected teams
